_what_this_is: the exact provider/account/credential/cost action a durable-backend decision needs, stated so the decision is a decision rather than a discussion. No paid external service was created.

what_is_already_built_and_costs_nothing._generic_means: it names no provider, protocol, bucket, region, endpoint, experiment, model family or parameter count -- a test asserts each of those. It defines four methods and composes them with the identity functions so no caller can transfer without re-identifying the ARRIVED bytes.
what_is_already_built_and_costs_nothing._backends_are_application_layer: LocalDirStore is a filesystem directory -- the dev box's canonical artifact store IS one, so it is not a test double. S3CompatibleStore takes endpoint, bucket and credential ENV NAMES as arguments and contains no vendor host; a second service is two different strings at the construction site.

negative_controls: one flipped byte in the stored object -> refused
restore into an occupied path -> refused
missing object -> raises rather than an empty restore
validated_end_to_end._throughput_here_is_not_a_network_rate: the local round trip measured 2984 MB/s up and 806 MB/s down. Those are page-cached filesystem copies and are NOT evidence about any network. What this validated is the mechanism and the identity.

what_is_still_missing.the_network_leg: no measured rate from a durable backend to a replacement pod exists, because no backend could be provisioned that a pod with the approved GPU could also reach. That measurement is what the continuation's hard bound needs, and it cannot be taken without an account.
what_is_still_missing._therefore: the continuation cannot be repriced for the backend path yet. The only priced transport remains the dev box uplink, and it does not fit.

the_exact_action_required.shape: any S3-API object store the dev box can write to while no accelerator is billing, and a pod can read from at datacenter bandwidth. The brand does not matter to the code; three properties do -- unbilled upload, fast download, and bytes that arrive unchanged.
the_exact_action_required._why_this_candidate: it is region-free, so it does not reintroduce the datacenter-overlap problem that closed the regional volume: the L40S datacenter does not have to be the storage datacenter. Its published pricing also charges no egress, which matters because the download leg happens once per continuation attempt.
the_exact_action_required._candidate_is_not_a_recommendation_of_a_: any S3-API service with those properties works and needs no code change. A self-hosted endpoint would too.
steps: 1. an account with an S3-API object store (none exists for this project)
3. one S3 API credential pair (access key id + secret)
4. the two values placed in the environment under names this repository chooses; they are never written into the repository

cost_estimate._storage: published R2 pricing is $0.015/GB/month, so ~23.85 GB for a few days is on the order of $0.05. UNVERIFIED: it is vendor-published, not measured, and cannot be confirmed without an account.
cost_estimate._egress: published as zero for R2; also unverified
cost_estimate._operations: about 100 PUTs and 100 GETs per continuation, which is negligible under any published operation pricing

what_it_buys.fill_leg: $0 of billed GPU time. The dev box uploads 22.2 GiB at its measured 0.64-0.72 MB/s -- about 9.5 hours of wall clock -- before any pod exists.
what_it_buys.drain_leg: minutes at datacenter bandwidth, UNMEASURED until a backend exists. It must be measured and used as the bound; a published figure must not be.
what_it_buys._and_R2_is_preserved: the bytes travel unchanged and are re-identified on arrival at the new local path, which is the same check the scp path performs and the same one the generic interface now makes unavoidable.

what_was_NOT_done: no paid external service was authorized or used
no credential was created or stored
